originalTitle: Cancer vaccine from Moderna, Merck shows promise in late-stage trial; both stocks soar
summary: The combination regimen significantly extended the time patients lived without their melanoma returning, compared with Keytruda alone.
content:
An experimental personalized cancer vaccine from Merck and Moderna showed positive initial results in its first-ever late-stage trial, the companies announced Wednesday, bringing them one step closer to filing for approval of the treatment option.

The mRNA-based shot in combination with Merck's immunotherapy Keytruda met key goals in the Phase 3 trial in more than 1,100 patients with higher-risk or advanced melanoma whose detectable cancer had been completely removed through surgery.

Merck shares climbed more than 12% on Wednesday, while Moderna's stock soared about 177%. The size of those moves reflect the companies' relative size entering Wednesday: Merck's market cap was around $333 billion, while Moderna's sat near $25 billion.

The combination regimen met the main study goal of significantly extending the time patients lived without their melanoma returning, compared with Keytruda alone. The treatment also reduced the risk of the cancer spreading to distant parts of the body. Those results build on positive Phase 2 trial data on the same regimen earlier this year.

"It's a big moment for medicine, a big moment for patients," Moderna CEO Stephane Bancel said in an interview on CNBC's " Squawk Box ."

The Phase 3 study will continue to assess other outcomes, including the overall survival benefit of the regimen. The drugmakers plan to present the data at an upcoming international medical meeting, but it's unclear when they plan to submit applications for approval in the U.S.

The drugmakers will likely start talking to regulatory agencies about the treatment and its safety "in the next few months," Dr. Dean Li, president of Merck Research Laboratories, told "Squawk Box."

The initial data suggests that the combo could serve as a new treatment option for melanoma, which accounts for only about 1% of skin cancers but causes the large majority of deaths among them. Most recurrences of melanoma develop in the first two to three years after initial treatment and removal.

Melanoma patients are "stuck having to deal with the new gravity of that diagnosis and then undergo uncomfortable treatments like surgery, and after that, they're worried about their cancer coming back," Dr. Jane Healy, Merck's head of oncology early development, said in an interview.

She called it "very exciting" that the therapy led to a "clinically meaningful improvement" over Keytruda – the standard of care for melanoma – and was well tolerated by patients. Side effects were similar to other vaccines that people typically get for other diseases, Healy noted.

The results also validate a personalized treatment approach that Merck and Moderna have been developing for decades, she added.

Every tumor has a unique set of mutations, even among patients with the same type of cancer, Healy said. Merck and Moderna's personalized vaccine is designed to target the specific mutations in each patient's tumor rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach. The idea is to train the immune system to recognize and kill those unique cancer markers and then pair that response with Keytruda, which helps the body attack the cancer more effectively.

"We think [the results are] very meaningful for patients with this disease and really the potential of what it can mean for other patients for cancer in future trials with this particular new class of therapy," she said.

In a June note ahead of the results, Leerink Partners analyst Mani Foroohar said the Phase 3 results are a make-or-break event for Moderna's stock.

Analysts said the company's valuation already reflected expectations that the personalized cancer vaccine could eventually work across multiple types of cancers – not just melanoma — before Wednesday's stock move.

Merck and Moderna are studying the vaccine in several trials across other tumors, such as non-small cell lung cancer, bladder cancer and renal cell carcinoma.
chineseTitle: 默克公司 Moderna 的癌症疫苗在后期试验中显示出希望；两只股票都飙升
chineseSummary: 与单独使用 Keytruda 相比，联合疗法显着延长了患者黑色素瘤不复发的生存时间。
chineseContent:
默克和莫德纳公司周三宣布，一种实验性个性​​化癌症疫苗在其首次后期试验中显示出积极的初步结果，使他们距离申请批准该治疗方案又近了一步。

基于 mRNA 的注射剂与默克公司的免疫疗法 Keytruda 相结合，在 1,100 多名高危或晚期黑色素瘤患者的 3 期试验中达到了关键目标，这些患者的可检测到的癌症已通过手术完全切除。

周三默克股价上涨超过 12%，Moderna 股价飙升约 177%。这些变动的规模反映了周三各公司的相对规模：默克公司的市值约为 3,330 亿美元，而 Moderna 的市值约为 250 亿美元。

与单独使用 Keytruda 相比，联合治疗方案达到了显着延长患者黑色素瘤不复发的生存时间的主要研究目标。该治疗还降低了癌症扩散到身体远处部位的风险。这些结果建立在今年早些时候相同方案的 2 期试验积极数据的基础上。

Moderna 首席执行官斯蒂芬·班塞尔 (Stephane Bancel) 在接受 CNBC 节目“Squawk Box”采访时表示：“这对医学、对患者来说都是一个重要时刻。”

第三阶段研究将继续评估其他结果，包括该疗法的总体生存获益。制药商计划在即将召开的国际医学会议上展示这些数据，但目前尚不清楚他们计划何时在美国提交批准申请。

默克研究实验室总裁 Dean Li 博士告诉“Squawk Box”，制药商可能会“在未来几个月内”开始与监管机构讨论该疗法及其安全性。

初步数据表明，该组合可以作为黑色素瘤的新治疗选择，黑色素瘤仅占皮肤癌的 1% 左右，但却导致了其中绝大多数死亡。大多数黑色素瘤复发是在初次治疗和切除后的头两到三年内发生的。

默克肿瘤学早期开发负责人简·希利博士在接受采访时表示，黑色素瘤患者“不得不应对诊断带来的新的严重性，然后接受手术等不舒服的治疗，之后，他们担心癌症会复发”。

她称“非常令人兴奋”的是，该疗法比 Keytruda（黑色素瘤的治疗标准）带来了“临床上有意义的改善”，并且患者耐受性良好。希利指出，副作用与人们通常为其他疾病接种的其他疫苗类似。

她补充说，这些结果还验证了默克和 Moderna 数十年来开发的个性化治疗方法。

希利说，每种肿瘤都有一组独特的突变，即使是患有相同类型癌症的患者也是如此。默克和 Moderna 的个性化疫苗旨在针对每位患者肿瘤的特定突变，而不是采用一刀切的方法。这个想法是训练免疫系统识别并杀死那些独特的癌症标记物，然后将这种反应与Keytruda配对，从而帮助身体更有效地攻击癌症。

她说：“我们认为，[结果]对于患有这种疾病的患者非常有意义，而且在未来使用这种特殊的新型疗法的试验中，它对其他癌症患者也具有潜在的意义。”

Leerink Partners 分析师 Mani Foroohar 在 6 月份发布的报告中表示，第三阶段的结果对于 Moderna 的股票来说是一个决定成败的事件。

分析师表示，在周三股价走势之前，该公司的估值已经反映了这种个性化癌症疫苗最终可能适用于多种癌症（而不仅仅是黑色素瘤）的预期。

默克和 Moderna 正在针对其他肿瘤（例如非小细胞肺癌、膀胱癌和肾细胞癌）进行多项试验来研究该疫苗。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
